references.label: Ministry of Development Provisional Order Confirmation (Bangor Borough Extension) Act (Northern Ireland) 1966 (1966 c. ii)
references.note: Local Act confirming the Bangor Borough (Extension) Order (Northern Ireland) 1966. Royal Assent 6 Dec 1966 (Belfast Gazette issue 2394, 9 Dec 1966, page 465). Appointed day 1 Apr 1967, as printed in the confirmed Order. Bangor borough extended; its Princetown, Dufferin, Castle, Clifton and Ballyholme wards were extended.

references.label: New Towns (Municipal Functions - Craigavon) Order (Northern Ireland) 1967 (S.R. & O. 1967 No. 57)
references.note: Made under section 28 of the New Towns Act (Northern Ireland) 1965; notice in Belfast Gazette issue 2411, 31 Mar 1967, page 111. From 1 Apr 1967 the Craigavon Development Commission acts as an urban district council for the whole of Lurgan Rural District except Ballyblagh, Knocknashane, Tirsogue and part of Toberhewny, which are added to the Borough of Lurgan; that area is known as the Urban District of Craigavon. The new town was designated by the New Town Designation Order (Northern Ireland) 1965 (Belfast Gazette issue 2317, 6 Aug 1965, page 274), which did not itself alter district boundaries.

references.label: Map of the Borough of Bangor as extended by the Bangor Borough (Extension) Order (Northern Ireland) 1966 (PRONI VAL/8/283)
references.note: Certified copy (Town Clerk, 5 Jan 1967; Valuation Office stamp 6 Jan 1967) on OSNI six-inch Co. Down sheets 1 and 2, revision of 1939. The borough line is the inner edge of the map's boundary band, registered on OSNI six-inch County Series Co. Down sheets 1, 2, 5 and 6, Edition 5 (revised 1938, 1939, 1938-39 and 1920 & 1939), about 20 m; townland lines where the band follows one. The added areas are given to wards by the map's colours (Order art. 4).

approximateSegments.note: Some lines on this map are approximate: parts of the Bangor borough boundary are taken from the council's 1965 map of the existing boundary or the map of the 1966 Order, registered on the OSNI six-inch Edition 5 sheets (about 20-25 m); parts of the other town and ward lines are traced from the maps deposited with their Orders (about 20-25 m); the Lisburn rural district lines of 1963 along the Glen, Shaw's and Stewartstown roads are drawn to about 150 m; Newtownabbey's line against the rural districts follows whole townlands read from a small-scale scheme map and is not confirmed. They are drawn dotted on the map.
